approachQuestion.prompt:
A late route closure

A route map stores n closed blocked sections [start,end], sorted by start and already separated: end[i] < start[i+1]. A new closed section [a,b] must be included. Return a new sorted list of maximal closed blocked sections covering exactly the old sections and the new one. Sections sharing an endpoint must become one section. Do not modify the input or reuse mutable input records as output records.

Input: sections = [[1,3],[7,9],[12,14]], added = [3,12]
Output: [[1,14]]
The added section touches the first and last sections and covers the middle one.

Input: sections = [], added = [5,5]
Output: [[5,5]]

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; all endpoints are integers between 0 and 1000000000; start ≤ end and a ≤ b. Singleton sections are legal. The lists support constant-time indexed reads. Choose the method with the best worst-case running time, then the least auxiliary memory; exclude the required new output from auxiliary memory.

options.text: Copy sections ending before a to the result. Keep a pending section initially [a,b]; while the next start is at most its current end, extend the pending end and start as needed. Emit the pending section, then copy all remaining sections.
options.feedback: The ordered, separated input gives a prefix before the new section, one connected block to combine, and an untouched suffix. The pending boundary must grow as it absorbs sections.

options.text: Copy all sections and the new section into a temporary array, sort it with comparison merge sort, and combine touching or overlapping sections into a separate result.
options.feedback: This is correct for every legal input and recognizes the need to combine connected coverage, but sorting again discards the useful order already provided.

options.text: Copy the prefix before a; combine only sections whose start is at most the original b, then emit the remaining sections unchanged.
options.feedback: Existing sections are separated. If a section extends beyond b, no later section can begin before that extended end. Thus testing starts against the original b absorbs exactly the same sections; extending the reported end still preserves the full coverage.

options.text: Use the three-region scan, but combine only when the next start is strictly less than the pending end.
options.feedback: Closed sections share an included boundary. For sections [[4,6]] and added [1,4], this keeps two records instead of the required single [1,6].

feedback.reason: Use existing separation to insert one section without re-sorting; distinguish closed endpoint contact from a gap.
details: Use a single forward index. Copy the separated prefix into new output records, extend one pending section through every touching or overlapping section, emit it, and copy the suffix. Append into a preallocated output array of n+1 slots with a logical result length; do not build a temporary copy.

Sorted disjoint old sections permit three phases: separated prefix, one expanding pending union, and separated suffix. Extending the pending end may pull further sections into that union; do not stop after the first overlap.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For three-region-insertion, n is the number of existing sections. The output array has capacity n+1 and a logical length, so no trimming copy is made; the whole returned array is output space. What is the tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair?
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)
Time O(log n), auxiliary space O(1)

feedback.reason: One forward index consumes old sections and writes new returned records.
details: The index advances through each old section at most once, including copying the unaffected suffix. A worst case returns n+1 records, so linear work is necessary. Only an index and pending boundaries are temporary. The separate returned records and their array are output space.
Iterative scan, preallocated returned output, no input copy or recursive calls.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The input is already sorted; the scan does not sort or allocate a sorting copy. Each old record is visited once.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The returned records are output space. Only indices and pending endpoints are auxiliary, so linear auxiliary memory overcounts the result.
“Time O(log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: Finding an insertion boundary is not the whole task: this method visits and copies the old sections, including a potentially linear unaffected suffix.
